name: Gavin Newsom
role: Governor of California (2019-present); Lieutenant Governor (2011-2019); Mayor of San Francisco (2004-2011)
summary: Newsom is a Democratic governor whose record is progressive on abortion, same-sex marriage, guns, climate and the death penalty, while on taxes on the wealthy, regulation of AI and fiscal limits on health coverage for undocumented immigrants he has taken more business-friendly or cautious positions. Many of his stances come from bills he signed or vetoed rather than from long statements.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mixed record: signed Healthy San Francisco (2007) and expanded Medi-Cal to low-income adults regardless of immigration status (2022 budget), but walked back support for single-payer in 2022 and in 2025 capped new enrolment of undocumented adults.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Signed the $20 fast-food minimum wage (AB 1228, 2023), citing fairer wages. A sector wage, not a general statewide increase.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Opposes California's billionaire tax (Prop 40) and opposed Prop 30 (2022) on state-level wealth/high-income taxes, citing tax-base flight, yet proposes a national minimum tax on net worth above $100 million.

unions-good.rationale: Signed the farmworker unionization law, saying farmworkers 'have the fundamental right to unionize'; in 2025 said he works to 'support labor unions and expand access to good jobs' and that what is good for workers is good for business. He also vetoed some labor-backed bills, and made no direct statement that unions benefit society.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Signed SB 53 (AI transparency rules) and oil price-gouging oversight with profit-penalty authority, but vetoed SB 1047 as too stringent and says regulation must not stifle industry.

cut-welfare.rationale: He proposes expanded social provision but enacted significant targeted healthcare reductions.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Supported Prop 64 (adult cannabis legalization) but vetoed SB 58 (psychedelics decriminalization, 2023) before treatment guidelines existed, while backing therapeutic use, and vetoed SB 57 (supervised injection sites, 2022) as lacking limits and vetted plans while leaving room for a limited pilot.

limit-guns.rationale: Proposed a 28th Amendment (age 21, universal background checks, waiting period, assault weapon ban) and signed many gun laws; says he supports civilian ownership but not current laxity.

rehabilitation.rationale: Announced in 2023 that San Quentin would become the San Quentin Rehabilitation Center, 'the nation's most innovative rehabilitation facility', pursuing 'true rehabilitation, justice, and safer communities'. He did not set it against punishment in those words, and has also backed tougher penalties for some property crime.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Directed San Francisco to issue same-sex marriage licences in 2004 citing equal protection; opposed Prop 8.

abortion-legal.rationale: Declared California an abortion sanctuary, signed insurance-coverage and shield measures, and said 'We will defend your constitutional right to make decisions about your own health.'

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Signed SB 518 (bureau to implement reparations eligibility), backed a state apology, and created the task force process, but vetoed cash-adjacent and ancestry-based bills in 2024-25 as unworkable or legally risky.

limit-growth.rationale: He explicitly rejects sacrificing economic growth to decarbonize.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Issued Executive Order N-79-20 requiring zero-emission new car sales by 2035, calling it the most impactful step the state can take against climate change. Later also signed oil-friendly SB 237.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Proposed raising federal inheritance taxes among a package of national taxes on the wealthy (reported 2026); amount of taxation not specified.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Sued over Trump's tariffs, saying they are 'wreaking chaos on California families, businesses and economy, driving up prices and threatening jobs'.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He advocates national industrial policy for the AI economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

democracy-best.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

political-violence-never.rationale: He condemned violent and destructive acts at the 2025 Los Angeles protests and said Trump tolerates violence that serves him; he did not say that political violence is never justified, so +1.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He explicitly rejects ancestry-based American identity and ethnonationalism.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: He supports land returns and tribal stewardship but vetoed expanded authority over ancestral waters and sacred sites.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 2025 said he has 'deep respect for the right of the State of Israel to exist and defend itself'. He did not use 'Jewish state' wording, and later criticized Israeli leadership and said the 'apartheid state' label could be applied appropriately (2026), so the match is partial.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Signed Medi-Cal expansion to undocumented adults (2019-2022 budgets). The 2025 enrolment freeze for new adult applicants was framed as a budget cap ('We're just capping it'), not as reserving benefits for citizens; existing enrollees and emergency care continue. Medi-Cal is health coverage rather than cash welfare.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Mixed: signed SB 237 (2025) allowing up to 2,000 Kern County drilling permits a year, while committing to phase out oil extraction by 2045 and seeking an end to new fracking permits.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He advocates equal civil rights across race, religion and class.

separated-powers.rationale: He explicitly calls for restored legislative checks and balances.

death-penalty.rationale: Declared a moratorium in 2019, said the intentional killing of another person is wrong and he would not oversee any execution; backed repeal measures in 2012 and 2016 and began dismantling death row.

flat-income-tax.rationale: He explicitly favors progressive taxation over regressive tax structures.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He insists even the president remains subject to law.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: He calls for concrete responses to boys’ suicide and isolation.

corporate-influence.rationale: He says decades of tax loopholes were written by lobbyists for the wealthy; this concerns wealthy interests rather than corporations specifically, so +1.

socialized-care.rationale: He proposes funding universal child care as part of a national compact; this is a proposal covering childcare only, not housework, so low.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He defends peaceful protest and criticises Trump's disregard for checks, but did not speak directly to suppressing opposition, so -1.

participatory-democracy.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Signed SB 107 (refuge for trans youth) and the SAFETY Act protecting students' gender identity privacy. He separately called trans athletes in women's sports unfair.

assisted-dying.rationale: Signed SB 380 (2021) easing access to the End of Life Option Act and SB 403 (2025) removing its expiry date.

social-market-economy.rationale: He combines entrepreneurship with regulation, arguing guardrails enable investment.

online-participation.rationale: Authored 'Citizenville' (2013) on digital tools for democratic participation and backed the Digital Democracy legislative-tracking tool. Source text not read in full.

open-government-data.rationale: Backed the Digital Democracy tool (2015) for following legislative proceedings; limited detail.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He argues concentrated wealth undermines democratic government.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Rejected eliminating police in 2020 ('If you're calling for eliminating police, no') and in 2021 said 'Don't ever confuse me with the defund police movement'. His San Quentin plan keeps prisons but changes their purpose.

rent-control.rationale: Signed AB 1482 (2019), a statewide cap of 5% plus inflation on annual rent increases with just-cause eviction rules, but opposed Prop 33 (2024), which would have expanded local rent control. Evidence points both ways.

recognise-genocide.rationale: As governor he issued a 2019 proclamation declaring a Day of Remembrance of the Armenian Genocide; a formal recognition of one case, so medium.

spiritual-nature.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

dense-cities.rationale: Signed SB 79 (2025) allowing 5-9 story housing near transit stops, saying homes near transit would reduce traffic and pollution as well as lower housing costs.

free-public-college.rationale: In a June 2026 op-ed he proposed a federal compact that would make higher education and career training free; it is a proposal tied to a national tax he has not enacted, so +1.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: He supports expanded earned-income and young-child tax credits.

voter-id.rationale: He opposes the citizenship-and-identification ballot measure.

notes:
Views shifted on Medi-Cal for undocumented adults (expanded 2022, capped 2025) and on trans athletes (2025 podcast). Research relied on official releases and news reports; his speeches, book and podcast transcripts were not available as full text, so most statements stay null.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 29 answers taken from it, 21 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass using saved full texts, not copied answers. Reviewed all 490 statements and every remaining null. State-of-the-State and UN remarks were read in full; the assembly also publishes the former as a PDF. The entire Pod Save America interview was read, with advertisements and host questions excluded. The Klein interview was downloaded after headless rendering; topic passages were read from its actual transcript, not its AI-generated notes; some letter speaker labels also mark archival Wilson clips, which were excluded. His faith is used only where he expressly links spiritual belonging to public justice, not to infer particular doctrines. His new federal tax proposal differs from his opposition to California asset taxes; neither cancels the other. The healthcare freeze and benefit reductions qualify his universal-coverage rhetoric. His current oil-well policy answers the fossil-production statement despite climate rhetoric. Diablo Canyon’s extension was checked but continuation alone does not establish expansion of nuclear capacity. Indigenous land returns and stewardship are weighed with the 2026 water and sacred-site vetoes. Proportional representation and equal electoral competition are not inferred from his support for partisan redistricting. Opposition to the Iran war and advocacy of congressional war authorization do not establish defensive-wars-only or a UN-approval rule. Calls for cooperation with China do not establish the statement’s separate preference for relying on China rather than the United States. No inference from party, family, office or a guest’s views. No inferred answers. Source reports of enacted policy remain medium; high confidence is confined to directly inspected orders or formal recognition. Any salience-only rejection is accepted. The SB 107 message was downloaded and OCR-read. Generic international cooperation does not settle the priority of national versus global interests, and opposition to military policing does not by itself establish a position on military constitutional guardianship; both remain null. The original March 2026 Politico interview could not be fetched; secondary reproductions were treated as leads only.
